analysis.evidence: Terah takes Abram, Lot, and Sarai, each introduced by the direct-object marker אֶת. The following clause says they set out from Ur for Canaan, showing that Terah took his relatives with him on the journey.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol. The verb is third person masculine singular, agreeing with its subject תֶּרַח.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקַּח תֶּרַח אֶת אַבְרָם בְּנוֹ reads “Terah took Abram his son.” The object marker אֶת introduces Abram, and בְּנוֹ identifies him as Terah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “he took.”
analysis.sense: The father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clear the unsupported root אבה and its link to article 2bh. Preserve the explanation of the compound name and its recorded bearer.
draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 identifies Abram as Terah’s son, and Genesis 17:5 records his change of name. The first element of אַבְרָם is the noun אָב, “father.” Neither verse supports deriving the name from אָבָה, “be willing.”

analysis.evidence: Terah is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “took.” In אֶת אַבְרָם בְּנוֹ, “Abram his son,” בְּנוֹ identifies Abram as Terah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת marks it as a direct object of וַיִּקַּח.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham
